summary.text: I build the operational backbone that teams rely on but rarely notice — the reports that run themselves, the SOPs people actually follow, the coordination that keeps 1,000-person events from falling apart backstage. At Home Digital Indonesia, I rebuilt a weekly reporting pipeline in Excel that gave the team back 12+ hours they were losing to manual data work. Before that, I ran a 34-member student council across 10 divisions on KPIs and weekly check-ins — not because it was trendy, but because nothing else was working. Currently studying Data Science at Universitas Terbuka, which shapes how I think about evidence, process, and what 'good enough' actually looks like in practice.

details: Rebuilt the daily sprint dashboards from scratch so every segment could see their own numbers in real time — no more waiting for someone to compile them.
Overhauled how we manage call frequency (CFM) across all 31 depots in West Java. The old system was slow and inconsistent; the new one actually matches what the field teams need.
Built an analytics dashboard for the Route-to-Market (RTM) division that covers every outlet and segment across the depot network. First time the team had all their data in one place.
Set up automated reports in Excel that cut about 12 hours of copy-paste work out of the team's week.
Wrote shared SOPs for Finance, Sales, and Ops — before that, each department had their own way of doing the same thing.
Used internal feedback data to flag process bottlenecks. Turned those into concrete proposals that management actually acted on.
Checked and maintained all safety gear on a regular schedule — ropes, harnesses, carabiners, the works.
Acted as lead climber and belayer during technical rescue training sessions.
Helped deliver hands-on instruction and ran skill tests for new trainees.
Ran a 34-person council across 10 divisions. Introduced KPIs because without them nobody knew which divisions were actually delivering.
Designed school-wide programs that the administration ended up keeping even after my term.
Led outreach campaigns to 12 feeder schools to get more students involved.
Set up weekly coordination check-ins between divisions — simple, but it stopped things from falling through the cracks.
Handled backstage coordination for events with 1,000+ people in the audience — lighting, sound, security, all moving at once.
Tightened transition times between segments by giving every crew a clear sequence to follow.

impact.title: Reporting Automation System

impact.title: KPI-Based Governance Leadership
impact.desc: I ran our student council (34 people, 10 divisions) with actual KPIs and weekly sync-ups. The programs we built got adopted by the school itself, and our outreach hit 12 feeder schools.
